public_rationale: Section 4.2 does not expressly make release conditional on government approval after reporting. That supports Marcus's underlying concern. But disclosure does not itself grant permission to release a risky product: the order preserves applicable law and existing agency authority. Because the wording moves from absence of an approval gate to freedom to release, the broader assertion is not established. The narrower FDA comparison is supported separately.
limitations: The result depends materially on what free to release means.
No actual product, risk finding or other applicable legal regime is specified.
Absence of an express release prohibition is not affirmative legal authorization.

criteria.support_condition: The foundation-model reporting provisions contain no release veto or prior-approval requirement triggered by disclosed risks, while other legal duties remain applicable.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Those provisions require approval or prohibit release because of the disclosed risks. An explicit preservation of other laws contradicts only an unrestricted reading that disclosure guarantees lawful release.
